keyword: is artemis 2 landing on the moon

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is not landing on the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Artemis II won’t land on the moon" (R1); "The crew on the 10-day mission won't land on the Moon" (R2); "The Artemis II crew will not land on the moon" (R3); "While Artemis II will not land on the moon" (R5); "sending astronauts on a 10-day voyage around the Moon and back" without landing (R6); "The quartet won't touch down on the lunar surface" (R7); "hurtle around Earth's nearest celestial neighbour without landing" (R8); "astronauts prepared... to return to the moon, but this time, they will not land" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly state no landing on Artemis II, directly supporting the claim.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is a 10-day crewed test flight designed to fly around the Moon and return to Earth to test systems for future missions.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Scheduled for almost 10 days, Artemis II won’t land... send humans around the moon" to test systems (R1); "historic 10-day mission around the Moon" crewed test (R2); "mission will last approximately 10 days... test... systems" around moon (R3); "10-day journey around the moon and back... vital test flight" (R5); "10-day voyage around the Moon and back... testing... Orion, and... Space Launch System" (R6); "10-day loop around the moon and back to Earth" test mission (R7); "approximately 10-day mission and hurtle around... without landing" test rocket/spacecraft (R8); "fly past the moon on a 10-day mission... critical test" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently describe it as ~10-day crewed test flying around Moon to test systems and return.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission's crew will fly near the lunar far side.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "slingshot around the moon... between 5,000 and 9,000 nautical miles beyond the far side of the moon" (R1); "fly at altitudes between 6,000 and 9,000 kilometers above the surface of the far side of the moon" (R3); "fly as close as 8,000 kilometers... from the lunar surface before swinging back around... far side of the Moon" (R6); "loop around the moon" far side (R7); "free-return trajectory... around the far side of the moon" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Direct mentions of flying near or beyond the far side of the Moon.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission's crew will reach record distances from Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "This crew will travel farther than any humans ever have before" (R1); "travelling further from Earth than anyone has ever been before... set a new record for the farthest" (R2, R6)
verifications.reasoning: Explicit statements that it sets new distance records from Earth.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission's crew will return for a splashdown.

verifications.claim: The objective of the Artemis II mission is to test the Orion capsule and Space Launch System (SLS) with humans on board.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Artemis I tested... SLS and Orion... NASA SLS rocket... demonstrate... technological capability" (R3); "testing the astronauts’ crew capsule, Orion, and their launch vehicle, the Space Launch System" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Precise matches naming Orion and SLS testing with crew.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is a flyby or loop mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "slingshot around the moon... circling it in a figure eight" (R1); "circle it" (R2); "circle it" loop (R3); "around the moon" (R5); "voyage around the Moon" (R6); "loop around the moon" (R7); "journey around the Moon" (R8); "lunar flyby... around the far side" (R9)

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is launched in April 2026.

verifications.claim: The first crewed landing of the Artemis program is currently slated for Artemis III/IV.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "That feat is reserved for Artemis IV and V, currently scheduled for 2028" (R1); "that will happen on Artemis IV" (R3); "Artemis IV landing in 2028" (R5); "land astronauts on the Moon with Artemis IV in 2028" (R6); "first moon landing... on Artemis 4" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Recent sources confirm first landing now on Artemis IV; claim's III/IV range accommodates prior/planned shifts without contradiction.
